title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Loire and eating with it

steps.title: Reading labels
steps.body: Most Loire labels name the appellation, not the grape. Sweetness terms help for Chenin: sec, dry; demi-sec, off-dry; moelleux, sweet; doux, very sweet. Sur lie marks lees-aged Muscadet. Crémant de Loire and Saumur Brut mark traditional method sparkling wine.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Muscadet suits oysters and mussels. Sancerre suits goat's cheese, like crottin de Chavignol, and fish. Vouvray demi-sec suits pork and spicy food. Chinon suits charcuterie, rillettes and roast chicken, served slightly cool. Sweet Layon suits fruit tarts and blue cheese.

steps.prompt: Which Loire cheese is a classic match for Sancerre?
steps.explanation: Crottin de Chavignol is a goat's cheese from a Sancerre village.

steps.body: The Loire is one of France's best sources of value. Cabernet Franc from Chinon and Muscadet sur lie offer real character at modest prices.

steps.prompt: Order these Loire terms from driest to sweetest.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Loire labels name places; learn the grapes
Sec to doux mark Chenin's sweetness
Muscadet with oysters, Sancerre with goat's cheese
